cases.reply:
Thank you for asking before falling behind on it — that's the right order to do this in.

Splitting an invoice into instalments is a change to your payment terms, and that decision is not mine to make or even to start on. Payment terms belong to **Eileen Hart, Finance and Billing** (non-standard terms and anything involving a repayment plan end with her, as owner). I have no billing tool or approval I can use to agree instalments, and I have not logged or sent this request anywhere: nothing has been passed on to Eileen from my side.

The handbook I work from doesn't list a direct email for Eileen. You can reach her through the company office, which is open Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 17:00, and the phones are answered there.

One thing I can say plainly: while the request is undecided, your invoice keeps its current terms and due date, and reminders would continue on our normal cadence. So it's worth reaching Eileen directly rather than waiting on this reply.

Instalment plans and changes to payment terms are not something I can agree or set up. Under the company's rules they belong to Eileen Hart, our Finance and Billing lead — she owns invoices, credit notes and payment terms, so she can look at invoice 1042 and decide whether splitting it over three months works.

I have raised your request with her as a review ticket, so it is with her now, marked that you asked to pay invoice 1042 in three monthly instalments rather than in full. I have not read or changed anything on the invoice, and nothing is agreed yet.

If you would like to speak to someone directly, the office is open Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 17:00, and the team can put you through to Eileen. In the meantime the invoice keeps its current due date and balance, and if it slips past due you will hear from us on the usual collections cadence.
